q: גבר בן 73 ,שמור קוגניטיבית, שנתיים לאחר אירוע מוחי עם חולשת פלג גוף ימין, פנה למלר\"ד בעקבות נפילה וחבלה לאגן. עד הנפילה התהלך עם הליכון. בצילום רנטגן: מה הטיפול המומלץ לפי המאמר Management of Acute Hip Fracture ?
o: רדוקציה של השבר בחדר ניתוח והשכבה עם מתיחה ל- 3 שבועות
ניתוח arthroplasty, תוך עד 48 שעות מהנפילה, וניוד מוקדם
בשל מגבלת ניידות מלפני הנפילה מומלץ להימנע מניתוח, מומלצת פיזיותרפיה וניוד מוקדם ככל האפשר
ניתוח מיסמור תוך לשדי (intramedullary nails)
explanation:
A displaced femoral-neck fracture can interrupt the blood supply to the head. This man walked with a frame before his fall and has function to regain. **Offer arthroplasty within 48 hours of the fracture when medically feasible, followed by early mobilization.**

**A. Reduction and three weeks of traction** — Traction leaves him immobile while the injured femoral head remains at risk of nonunion and osteonecrosis.
**B. Prompt arthroplasty and mobilization** — Panel B shows a displaced neck fracture. Replacing the head avoids dependence on healing of the displaced neck and supports weight bearing.
**C. Physiotherapy without surgery** — His previous stroke limited walking, but he could walk. That history alone gives no reason to forgo repair.
**D. Intramedullary nail** — A nail stabilizes unstable trochanteric or subtrochanteric fractures. This fracture lies within the capsule at the femoral neck.

Reference · Bhandari and Swiontkowski, Management of Acute Hip Fracture, 2017, pp. 2055 (Fig. 2B), 2057, 2059–2060.

q: בן 75, ברקע - מחלת לב איסכמית, MI לפני כ-5 שנים, מטופל ב- ASPIRIN. התקבל לאשפוז בעקבות דלקת ריאות. במהלך האשפוז, בעקבות פרפור פרוזדורים עם תגובה חדרית של 120, טופל בחוסמי ביטא וחזר לקצב סינוס. המטופל במשקל 70 ק"ג, בד"כ נייד בבית, נפל לפני כחצי שנה בביתו בעקבות היתקלות בשטיח, תפקודי כליה תקינים. מהו הטיפול התרופתי המומלץ בשחרורו?
o: הוספת טיפול ב- APIXABAN 2.5mg (ELIQUIS) פעמיים ביום
הפסקת טיפול ב-ASPIRIN והתחלת טיפול ב-APIXABAN 5mg (ELIQUIS) פעמיים ביום
הוספת טיפול ב-RIVAROXABAN 15mg (XARELTO) פעם ביום
המשך טיפול ב ASPIRIN בלבד
explanation:
An episode of atrial fibrillation during pneumonia can recur after recovery. At 75, a man with a prior infarction already has three CHA₂DS₂-VASc points. **Replace aspirin with apixaban 5 mg twice daily** for embolic prevention, given stable coronary disease, normal renal function and no indication for continuing an antiplatelet.

**A. Add low-dose apixaban** — His age is below 80, weight is 70 kg and renal function is normal. Adding aspirin also increases bleeding.
**B. Switch to full-dose apixaban** — The usual AF dose fits him. A single trip on a rug merits attention to fall hazards and does not remove the stroke-prevention benefit.
**C. Add rivaroxaban 15 mg** — This is a reduced AF dose for impaired renal clearance. Combining it with aspirin adds bleeding risk.
**D. Continue aspirin alone** — Aspirin treats platelet-mediated arterial events but offers insufficient protection against emboli from AF.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1202–1205, Tables 77-7 to 77-9. 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, §§6.8.2 and 10.10.

q: A 75-year-old woman has mixed urinary incontinence with both stress and urgency symptoms. Frequent urgency-related leakage bothers her much more than occasional stress leakage. Her postvoid residual is normal. Which initial treatment priority is appropriate?
o: Prioritize a surgical intervention for the stress component
Prioritize nonsurgical treatment for the stress component
Prioritize initial treatment for the urgency component
Give both components equal priority at the start of treatment
explanation:
Mixed incontinence combines pressure-related leakage and leakage preceded by urgency. **Start with the urgency component because it causes this patient the greater burden.**

**A. Prioritize a surgical intervention for the stress component** — Stress surgery would address her less troublesome symptom.
**B. Prioritize nonsurgical treatment for the stress component** — Pelvic-floor treatment can help stress leakage, but that is not her main concern.
**C. Prioritize initial treatment for the urgency component** — Urge suppression and bladder training target the frequent episodes she wants to reduce.
**D. Give both components equal priority at the start of treatment** — Both components deserve assessment, but equal initial treatment priority disregards her preference.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, p. 714.

q: אישה בת 80 עם דמנציה קלה, HTN, ו-UTIs חוזרים, גרה לבד. בנה מוצא אותה מבולבלת עם בגדים מלוכלכים במהלך ביקור. היא מאושפזת עם urosepsis, E. coli bacteremia, ו-AKI (Cr 2.8, baseline 1.0). לאחר טיפול, היא יציבה מבחינה רפואית אך מקבלת 18/30 ב-MMSE וזקוקה להשגחה לתרופות ולהיגיינה. הבן עובד במהלך היום. מתחיל תכנון שחרור. איזו אפשרות מאזנת בצורה הטובה ביותר בין האוטונומיה שלה לצרכי הבטיחות?
o: שחרור לבית עם home health aide יומי
הרשמה ל-PACE program עם נוכחות ב-day center
אשפוז קבוע בבית אבות
מעבר לגור עם הבן ו-adult day care
explanation:
לאחר אלח דם יש לבדוק מה השתנה מהתפקוד הקודם והאם בלבול שיורי משפיע על ההערכה. החלטה על מסגרת מצריכה תוכנית ממשית לתרופות, להיגיינה ולשעות שבהן האדם נשאר לבד.
**PACE ומרכז יום הם אפשרות לשימור המגורים בקהילה אם היא עומדת בתנאי הקבלה והצוות יכול להבטיח תוכנית בטוחה גם בערב ובלילה.**

**א. מטפל המבקר פעם ביום.** ביקור קצר משאיר ללא מענה שעות שבהן ייתכן צורך בהשגחה על נטילת תרופות או טיפול עצמי.
**ב. PACE ומרכז יום.** הצוות משלב מעקב רפואי עם עזרה אישית ויכול להתאים את היקף הטיפול לתפקוד לאחר ההחלמה.
**ג. אשפוז סיעודי קבוע.** ציון קוגניטיבי יחיד אחרי מחלה חריפה אינו מספיק להחלטה בלתי מוגבלת בזמן.
**ד. מגורים עם הבן ומרכז יום.** זו חלופה אם שניהם מעוניינים והבית מתאים. נכונותו לארח ויכולתו לספק עזרה לא תוארו.

אסמכתא · Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 238–241, 243. Medicare, PACE, Who can get PACE?
ref: Hazzard Ch 17 — COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE

q: אישה בת 79 במוסד סיעודי מפתחת דלקת ריאות אספירטיבית חוזרת. יש לה דמנציה וסקולרית בינונית (MMSE 18/30), סוכרת, ו-CKD שלב 3 (eGFR 45). התרופות הנוכחיות כוללות metformin 500 mg BID, amlodipine 5 mg ליום, ו-sertraline 50 mg ליום. בדיקת בליעה בווידאופלואורוסקופיה מראה אספירציה שקטה של נוזלים דקים. קלינאית התקשורת ממליצה על נוזלים מסומכים, אך המטופלת מסרבת. לבתה יש ייפוי כוח מתמשך. מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?
o: הנחת PEG tube לכל התזונה
דחיית סירוב המטופלת ואכיפת נוזלים מסומכים
דיון במטרות טיפול ובעדיפויות איכות החיים
הפסקת כל צריכה אורלית באופן מיידי
explanation:
סירוב למרקם מסוים מחייב לברר מה המטופלת מבינה ומה חשוב לה: הנאה ואיכות חיים, תזונה ובטיחות בליעה. מבררים גם אם ייפוי הכוח הופעל ומה היקפו. **דיון במטרות טיפול ובעדיפויות איכות החיים**.

**א. הנחת PEG tube לכל התזונה.** PEG אינו מתחייב מסירוב לנוזלים מסומכים.
**ב. דחיית סירוב המטופלת ואכיפת נוזלים מסומכים.** אין לכפות מרקם בלי לברר כשרות ורצון.
**ג. דיון במטרות טיפול ובעדיפויות איכות החיים.** שיחה על היעדים מאפשרת לדון בסיכוני שאיפה ובחלופות.
**ד. הפסקת כל צריכה אורלית באופן מיידי.** איסור מיידי גורף על אכילה אינו נובע מעצם הסירוב.

אסמכתא · חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8 בקובץ המקומי. המלצות הוועדה להזנה בחולים עם קיהיון, עמ׳ 5.

q: A 78-year-old woman develops postoperative delirium. She receives diphenhydramine for sleep and famotidine started during admission; neither has an ongoing essential indication. According to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, which medication-review approach is appropriate?
o: Consider stopping both drugs to reduce medication-related delirium risk
Consider retaining both drugs and adding lorazepam at night
Consider retaining diphenhydramine and adding zolpidem for sleep
Consider retaining famotidine and adding clonazepam at night
explanation:
Diphenhydramine is a strongly anticholinergic antihistamine. Famotidine is an H2 receptor blocker that can also contribute to confusion, particularly when clearance is reduced.
**Review stopping both unnecessary medicines and use environmental sleep measures.**

**A. Consider stopping both drugs to reduce medication-related delirium risk.** Both drugs have delirium-related cautions and neither has an ongoing indication here.
**B. Consider retaining both drugs and adding lorazepam at night.** Retaining both and adding lorazepam increases central drug exposure.
**C. Consider retaining diphenhydramine and adding zolpidem for sleep.** Adding zolpidem retains the anticholinergic and introduces another delirium-associated hypnotic.
**D. Consider retaining famotidine and adding clonazepam at night.** Clonazepam adds sedation without addressing an unnecessary H2 blocker.

Reference · AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Tables 3 and 7, pp. 2066, 2074

q: An 82-year-old man with mild dementia and treated depression has acquired a firearm for protection. His wife recently found him looking sad while holding the loaded gun. He denies suicidal thoughts and says he was checking the weapon. He takes sertraline and donepezil. Alongside immediate assessment of suicide risk, which action directly reduces access to lethal means?
o: Increase the antidepressant dose and arrange a later follow-up visit
Arrange a mental-health referral while leaving firearm access unchanged
Document firearm-storage advice while leaving firearm access unchanged
Work with family to remove access to the firearm temporarily
explanation:
Accessible lethal means increase immediate danger during a suicidal crisis. A concerning observation from a relative matters even when the patient denies intent, especially if cognitive impairment limits the history.
**Work with the family to remove his access to the firearm temporarily while arranging an urgent safety assessment.**

**A. Increase sertraline.** A dose change takes time to affect depression and leaves the immediate hazard in place.
**B. Arrange referral alone.** Specialist input is appropriate, but waiting for an appointment leaves access unchanged.
**C. Document advice alone.** Documentation records the conversation. Check that a safe arrangement actually removes access.
**D. Work with the family.** Coordinate a safe, lawful arrangement with appropriate help. If danger is immediate, seek emergency assistance and avoid putting family members in harm’s way.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1013, 1017–1018, Figure 65-3

q: A 75-year-old man with symptomatic lumbar spinal stenosis asks about epidural steroid injection. Which result matches the randomized trial in Hazzard comparing glucocorticoid plus lidocaine with lidocaine injection?
o: Little added short-term benefit compared with lidocaine injection
Substantial added short-term benefit compared with lidocaine injection
Little added short-term benefit compared with an uninjected control
Substantial added short-term benefit compared with decompressive surgery
explanation:
Epidural injections are used for leg pain from lumbar spinal stenosis. Both randomized groups received lidocaine, so the comparison isolated the contribution of the glucocorticoid. **Adding steroid offered little additional benefit at six weeks.**

**A. Little benefit beyond lidocaine.** The groups had similar outcomes for both leg pain intensity and pain-related disability.
**B. Substantial benefit beyond lidocaine.** At six weeks the groups differed by only 0.2 points in average leg pain on a scale from zero to ten.
**C. Little benefit over no injection.** Everyone received an epidural injection, leaving its benefit over no procedure unanswered.
**D. Substantial benefit over surgery.** Decompression relieves anatomic narrowing. The trial had no surgical comparison group.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1639. Friedly et al., N Engl J Med 2014, vol. 371, pp. 11–21.
ref: Hazzard Ch 102 — BACK PAIN AND SPINAL STENOSIS

q: An 81-year-old woman with diabetes receives insulin and a beta-blocker for cardiovascular disease. Which beta-blocker effect is relevant to hypoglycemia safety?
o: It may enhance the counterregulatory response to falling blood glucose
It may impair the counterregulatory response to falling blood glucose
It may strengthen adrenergic counterregulation during a fall in glucose
It may preserve adrenergic counterregulation during a fall in glucose
explanation:
Falling glucose activates the sympathoadrenal system, which contributes both warning symptoms and defenses against a further fall. Beta blockade can interfere with this response.

**A beta blocker may impair counterregulation during hypoglycemia.** Review symptoms, measured glucose and insulin dosing rather than relying on a pulse change to recognize a low.

**A. Enhances the response.** Blocking beta receptors does not strengthen the adrenergic defense.
**B. Impairs the response.** Reduced beta-adrenergic signaling can compromise recognition or the response to a low.
**C. Strengthens adrenergic counterregulation.** The drug blocks part of this pathway.
**D. Preserves adrenergic counterregulation.** Presuming a fully intact response overlooks the drug effect.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p1584.

q: A 77-year-old woman presents after a fall and reports a month of dizziness on standing. She takes amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, and lisinopril 20 mg each morning. Blood pressure is 138/78 supine and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 68 to 74. Potassium is 3.3 and creatinine 1.2. During medication review, which option both removes the thiazide exposure associated with potassium loss and provides potassium replacement?
o: Move all three antihypertensives to bedtime without changing the prescribed drugs
Stop hydrochlorothiazide and provide potassium replacement with repeat monitoring
Reduce all three antihypertensive doses without providing potassium replacement
Replace lisinopril with an ARB while continuing the other prescribed drugs
explanation:
A 30 mm Hg systolic fall on standing with dizziness is symptomatic orthostatic hypotension. Hydrochlorothiazide can contribute through volume and potassium losses. **Stop hydrochlorothiazide, replace potassium and recheck standing pressure, renal function and electrolytes.**

**A. Move all drugs to bedtime** — Changing the clock leaves the thiazide exposure and potassium loss in place and may aggravate nocturia.
**B. Stop the thiazide and replace potassium** — This removes the likely ongoing loss and addresses potassium of 3.3. Monitor replacement, especially while she takes lisinopril.
**C. Lower all doses without replacement** — She would remain exposed to the thiazide, and the plan gives no potassium replacement.
**D. Exchange lisinopril for an ARB** — The switch leaves the potassium-wasting drug in place and fails to correct the measured deficit.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1222–1223, 1225–1226, Table 79-4.

q: An independently mobile 81-year-old man has mild to moderate chronic constipation despite lifestyle changes. He drinks adequate fluids, has no suspected fecal impaction or obstruction, and has not tried laxatives. Which initial treatment fits the Hazzard stepwise approach?
o: Start daily oral docusate and review the bowel response
Start psyllium with fluids and review the bowel response
Start oral magnesium citrate and review the bowel response
Start daily enema treatment and review the bowel response
explanation:
Bulk-forming fiber increases stool volume and provides a stimulus to propulsion. It suits an ambulant person with mild or moderate constipation who can drink enough fluid.
**Start psyllium with adequate fluid and reassess.**

**A. Docusate.** It has less effect on stool consistency and frequency than psyllium.
**B. Psyllium.** Gradual introduction improves tolerance. Review for bloating and whether defecation becomes easier.
**C. Magnesium citrate.** A potent saline cathartic is excessive for uncomplicated initial treatment.
**D. Daily enemas.** There is no current impaction or outlet disorder to justify a regular rectal regimen.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1375, 1378, Table 87-11.

q: An 81-year-old woman with hyponatremia takes a thiazide and sertraline. Which approach to medication review follows the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Consider the thiazide contribution and decrease sodium-monitoring frequency
Consider both medications and monitor sodium when treatment is changed
Consider the sertraline contribution and decrease sodium-monitoring frequency
Consider the combination protective and continue treatment without sodium monitoring
explanation:
Thiazides and SSRIs can each contribute to hyponatremia. In a patient already affected, both medicines belong in the review.

**Assess the thiazide and sertraline and follow sodium closely when treatment changes.** The medication list alone cannot determine their relative contributions.

**A. Consider only the thiazide and check less often.** This omits the SSRI and relaxes monitoring despite existing hyponatremia.
**B. Consider both and monitor.** Reviewing both exposures and repeating sodium can help guide treatment safely.
**C. Consider only sertraline and check less often.** This overlooks the diuretic and could miss worsening hyponatremia.
**D. Assume the combination is protective.** Both medicines can contribute to lower sodium, so continuing without surveillance leaves the hazard unassessed.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2068.

q: איזה מבין ההיגדים הבאים נכון באשר ליעילות הטיפול התרופתי בדיכאון בזקנים?
o: יעילות הטיפול התרופתי בחולים הלוקים בדמנציה מוטלת בספק
יעילות הטיפול בפלצבו זניחה בקרב מטופלים זקנים
יעילות הטיפול התרופתי טובה יותר בקרב המאובחנים עם דיכאון קל לעומת דיכאון חמור
יעילות הטיפול התרופתי טובה יותר ככל שהטיטרציה במינון מהירה יותר
explanation:
Antidepressant benefit varies with the depressive syndrome and the clinical population. Symptoms such as apathy, withdrawal and poor appetite in dementia may have several causes.
**The average benefit of antidepressants for depression in dementia is uncertain, so define a treatment goal and reassess whether it is achieved.**

**A. Uncertain efficacy in dementia.** Negative trials limit confidence in a routine drug benefit. Caregiver support and tailored activities can improve mood and engagement.
**B. Negligible placebo response.** Many participants improve in placebo groups. This reduces the incremental effect attributable to the drug.
**C. Greater benefit in mild depression.** Evidence for added drug benefit is weaker at low symptom severity, especially for subsyndromal depression.
**D. Faster titration improves efficacy.** Gradual titration can improve adherence through fewer early adverse effects and closer contact. Faster escalation has no established advantage here.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1014–1015
